resource.name: aws_lambda_function_url
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_lambda_function_url` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of HTTPS endpoints for AWS Lambda functions, allowing users to invoke functions directly via a URL without requiring API Gateway. Common use cases include building lightweight serverless APIs, integrating Lambda with webhooks, or enabling public or private access to Lambda functions for event-driven workflows. Key configurations include setting authentication methods (e.g., IAM or none), defining CORS settings, and managing lifecycle policies for secure and scalable function access.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to retrieve an existing AWS Lambda Function URL using the `aws_lambda_function_url` data source by specifying the `function_name` variable. This example is useful for referencing and integrating the URL of an already deployed Lambda function in Terraform configurations."

arguments.name: authorization_type
arguments.llm_summary: The `authorization_type` argument for the `aws_lambda_function_url` resource specifies the authentication mechanism required to access the Lambda function's URL, allowing users to control whether the URL is publicly accessible (`NONE`) or requires AWS IAM-based authorization (`AWS_IAM`). Setting this argument directly impacts access control, enabling users to secure the function URL based on their application's security requirements.

arguments.name: function_name
arguments.description: (Required) The name (or ARN) of the Lambda function.
arguments.llm_summary: The `function_name` argument specifies the name or ARN of the Lambda function to associate with the `aws_lambda_function_url` resource, enabling users to define which function will be accessible via the generated HTTPS endpoint. By setting this argument, users establish the connection between the function and its public URL, supporting use cases like exposing serverless APIs or event-driven workflows.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_lambda_function_url` resource represents the unique identifier of the Lambda function URL, typically auto-generated by AWS. While not required to be explicitly set by the user, it allows referencing or retrieving the specific URL resource for integration, management, or tracking purposes within Terraform configurations.

arguments.name: invoke_mode
arguments.llm_summary: The `invoke_mode` argument for the `aws_lambda_function_url` resource allows users to specify how the Lambda function is invoked via its function URL, controlling the invocation behavior (e.g., synchronous or asynchronous execution). Configuring this argument impacts the request handling mode, enabling users to tailor the function's execution pattern to suit specific application requirements, such as real-time processing or decoupled workflows.

arguments.name: qualifier
arguments.llm_summary: The `qualifier` argument for the `aws_lambda_function_url` resource allows users to specify the version or alias of the associated Lambda function that the function URL will invoke, such as `"$LATEST"` or a named alias. By setting this argument, users can control which specific version or environment of the Lambda function is exposed via the function URL, enabling targeted deployments or version-specific access for their application.

blocks.name: cors

arguments.name: allow_credentials
arguments.llm_summary: The `allow_credentials` argument in the `cors` configuration for the `aws_lambda_function_url` resource specifies whether the `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` header is included in responses, enabling support for authenticated requests in cross-origin resource sharing (CORS). Setting this to `true` allows clients to send credentials (e.g., cookies or authentication tokens) with CORS requests, which is essential for applications requiring secure, stateful interactions across origins.

arguments.name: allow_headers
arguments.llm_summary: The `allow_headers` argument in the `cors` block of the `aws_lambda_function_url` resource allows users to specify a set of HTTP headers that are permitted in CORS requests to the Lambda function URL. By configuring this argument, users can control which headers client applications are allowed to include in their requests, ensuring compatibility with specific application requirements and enhancing security by restricting unauthorized headers.

arguments.name: allow_methods
arguments.llm_summary: The `allow_methods` argument in the `cors` block of the `aws_lambda_function_url` resource allows users to specify the HTTP methods (e.g., `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`) permitted for cross-origin requests to the Lambda function URL. Configuring this argument ensures fine-grained control over the allowed request types, supporting common user goals like securing API endpoints and enabling specific client interactions.

arguments.name: allow_origins
arguments.llm_summary: The `allow_origins` argument in the `cors` block of the `aws_lambda_function_url` resource specifies a set of allowed origin domains for cross-origin resource sharing (CORS). By configuring this argument, users can control which external domains are permitted to make requests to the Lambda function URL, enabling secure interaction between the function and web applications hosted on different origins.

arguments.name: expose_headers
arguments.llm_summary: The `expose_headers` argument in the `cors` configuration for the `aws_lambda_function_url` resource allows users to specify a set of HTTP headers that clients are permitted to access in the response from the Lambda function. By defining this argument, users can control which headers are exposed to browsers during cross-origin requests, enabling fine-grained customization of CORS behavior to meet application requirements for secure and compliant data sharing.

arguments.name: max_age
arguments.llm_summary: The `max_age` argument in the `cors` block of the `aws_lambda_function_url` resource specifies the maximum duration (in seconds) that a browser should cache the preflight response for CORS requests. Configuring this value helps optimize performance by reducing the frequency of preflight requests, aligning with user goals of improving application responsiveness and minimizing network overhead.

blocks.llm_summary: The "cors" configuration block within the "aws_lambda_function_url" resource defines Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) settings for the Lambda function's URL endpoint. It encapsulates related settings such as allowed origins, headers, methods, and credentials, enabling users to control access from external domains and ensure secure interaction between the Lambda function and client applications. Configuring this block helps users enforce fine-grained CORS policies to support web-based integrations while maintaining security and compliance.

blocks.name: timeouts

arguments.name: create
arguments.llm_summary: The `create` argument within the `timeouts` block for the `aws_lambda_function_url` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (as a string) Terraform should wait for the creation of a Lambda Function URL before timing out. Configuring this argument helps ensure predictable provisioning behavior, especially in scenarios where resource creation may take longer due to network latency or other factors.

blocks.llm_summary: The "timeouts" configuration block in the `aws_lambda_function_url` resource defines customizable time limits for specific operations, such as creating, updating, or deleting the Lambda function URL. By configuring this block, users can manage operation durations to prevent long-running tasks or timeout errors, ensuring smoother deployment and lifecycle management of Lambda function URLs.

attributes.name: function_url
attributes.description: HTTP URL endpoint for the function in the format `https://<url_id>.lambda-url.<region>.on.aws/`.
